q: When the solutions of an acid and a base are mixed, an acid-base neutralisation reaction occurs, forming ____ and water.
e: When the solutions of an acid and a base are mixed, an acid-base neutralisation reaction occurs, forming salt and water. Salt is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Salts are strong electrolytes that completely dissociate into ____ in water.
e: Salts are strong electrolytes that completely dissociate into ions in water. Ions is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Water solutions of normal salts may be acidic, basic, or neutral depending on the ____.
e: Water solutions of normal salts may be acidic, basic, or neutral depending on the salt. Salt is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The term ____ describes the reaction of an anion or a cation of a salt, or both with water.
e: The term salt hydrolysis describes the reaction of an anion or a cation of a salt, or both with water. Salt hydrolysis is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Salt hydrolysis usually affects the ____ of a solution.
e: Salt hydrolysis usually affects the pH of a solution. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: The cation $Na^+$ and the anion $Cl^-$ of the salt do not react with ____.
e: The cation Na+ and the anion Cl- of the salt do not react with water. Water is often the solvent, the proton host, or a condensation product, depending on the stem.

q: The ionic equilibrium of water remains ____.
e: The ionic equilibrium of water remains undisturbed. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Solutions of salts of strong bases and strong acids are therefore ____ (pH=7) because neither ion of such a salt disturbs the equilibrium of water.
e: Solutions of salts of strong bases and strong acids are therefore neutral (pH=7) because neither ion of such a salt disturbs the equilibrium of water. A strong base ionises completely in water and produces a high [OH-].

q: The cation $Na^+$ of the salt does not react with water. This is because the product base is so ____ so that no formation of molecule, NaOH, occurs.
e: The cation Na+ of the salt does not react with water. This is because the product base is so strong so that no formation of molecule, NaOH, occurs. Strong is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: On the other hand, the anion $CH_3COO^-$ of the salt is a strong ____ of the weak acid, $CH_3COOH$.
e: On the other hand, the anion CH3COO- of the salt is a strong conjugate base of the weak acid, CH3COOH. A conjugate base is what is left after an acid gives away a proton.

q: The cation $NH_4^+$ of the salt is a strong conjugate acid of the weak base ____.
e: The cation NH4+ of the salt is a strong conjugate acid of the weak base NH4OH. A conjugate acid is what you get when a base picks up a proton.

q: For a salt derived from a weak acid and a weak base, both the cation and the anion ____.
e: For a salt derived from a weak acid and a weak base, both the cation and the anion hydrolyse. Hydrolyse: a weak base ionises only a little in water.

q: If $K_b$ for the anion is greater than $K_a$ for the cation ($K_b > K_a$), then the solution must be ____ because the anion will react with water to a greater extent than the cation.
e: If Kb for the anion is greater than Ka for the cation (Kb > Ka), then the solution must be basic because the anion will react with water to a greater extent than the cation. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: Conversely, if $K_b$ for the anion is smaller than $K_a$ for the cation ($K_b < K_a$), the solution will be ____ because the cation will react with water to a greater extent than the anion.
e: Conversely, if Kb for the anion is smaller than Ka for the cation (Kb < Ka), the solution will be acidic because the cation will react with water to a greater extent than the anion. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: If $K_b$ for the anion is approximately equal to $K_a$ for the cation ($K_b \approx K_a$), the solution will be nearly ____ because the anion produces $OH^-$ ions just as the cation produces $H^+$ ions.
e: If Kb for the anion is approximately equal to Ka for the cation (KbKa), the solution will be nearly neutral because the anion produces OH- ions just as the cation produces H+ ions. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.
